title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Competence in New Areas
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal who strictly handles traffic tickets (POA) is approached by their best friend to represent them in a highly complex Commercial WSIB claim. The paralegal has zero experience in WSIB law. How can the paralegal ethically accept this retainer?
options: By agreeing to learn WSIB law on the fly, and charging the client an hourly rate for the time spent learning the new area of law.
By associating with or retaining a licensee who is competent in WSIB law, with the client's consent.
The paralegal cannot ethically accept the retainer under any circumstances.
By having the client sign a waiver acknowledging the paralegal's incompetence and absolving them of liability.
questions.explain: Under Rule 3.01 (Competence), a paralegal who lacks competence in a particular task may accept a retainer if they associate with or retain a licensee who is competent in that area (with client consent), or if they can become competent without undue delay, risk, or expense to the client. Charging the client for the paralegal's basic education in the law is an unethical expense.
